_note:
The conversation behind each study testbed's history, replayed post hoc by scripts/study/backfill_capture.py.

Why it is needed: the testbeds were built by replaying harvested agent sessions (scripts/study/harvest/), so no prompt hook was running while the commits were made and the capture stores ship empty. A participant in the sgt arm would then meet a tool whose most human attribute -- what each piece of work was asked for, in the words somebody typed -- is blank on every chapter, which is one of the things the arm is being evaluated on.

Where the words come from: each entry renders the REAL brief that drove that session, from scripts/study/harvest/roles-<project>.json, named in `brief`. The asks and their specifics are that brief's -- the February 2019 snowstorm, the busiest hour called out at the top, the totals that must not lose the event days -- because the code in the repository was produced by them, and words that merely sounded plausible would make every surface that quotes them a fiction.

What is staged: the SURFACE. A harvested brief is a clean stakeholder paragraph; a prompt typed at an agent is not. Each one is re-typed the way it would actually have been sent -- lower case, typos left in, the request buried after the reasoning, some of them long and unwieldy -- because a testbed of tidy one-line prompts would exercise none of what the reading surfaces have to do with a real one. Two kinds of turn are additions rather than renderings, and both are marked: `"question": true` is a turn that produced no code (it must own no edits), and a second speaking turn in a window is a correction (both turns then claim the part of the save they were followed by).

Keyed by commit SUBJECT, which survives a testbed rebuild where shas do not; `brief` is checked against the roles file by tests/test_study_prompts.py, so a fixture that drifted from the harvest fails at test time rather than shipping. The initial dashboard commit has no brief and gets none -- one save in each testbed carries no words at all, which is a state the surfaces have to be seen in.

prompts.text: so the committee paper needs a chart of what time of day people actually ride, which i cant get out of the csv by hand. can you add a page showing the average count for each hour of the day, and call out the busiest hour at the top so nobody has to read the chart to get the headline. link it from the nav as well

commuters and weekend riders are two different crowds and the paper treats them seperately, so the single line we have now describes neither of them. split the hour of day page so weekdays and weekends can be seen side by side. keep the combined view as well though, i still want it
does friday evening count as weekday or weekend for this? the shape looks more like a weekend to me but i dont know

there are days in here that are nothing like a normal day. the february 2019 snowstorm, christmas, the fourth of july, that sort of thing. start keeping track of which days those are so we can tell them apart later. theres a list in my email i will paste in later, for now put in the handful you can find by looking at the numbers and leave it easy to add more

add a page showing the total for each month back to the start of the file, as a chart. the point of it is to see the summer dip when the weather turns. put the highest and lowest month in words above the chart
on the daily and monthly charts, make the event days we track stand out from the ordinary ones, so nobody reads a spike as growth when it was a heat wave. however you think is clearest
hm no, not a shaded band behind the whole day, that made the chart look like it was broken. a small marker under the axis is enough

theres a sensor on each side of the bridge and people keep asking me whether the two sides are balanced, which i cant answer. add a page comparing east and west: totals for each, and how the split changes across the hours of the day
i need a page with one row per year: total, average day, busiest day and its date. this is the table that goes at the front of the paper

ok this is the one thats been bugging me for weeks. the averages are being pulled around by the event days -- a snowbound monday is not what an average sunday looks like, and the quiet-day figure we quoted in the report is basically wrong because of it. keep them out of the averages wherever we show one, but do not lose them from the totals or the daily table, the totals are what the funding number is built on and dropping a real ride out of a total would be misreporting. and it has to be the same rule on every page, i dont want the monthly page doing one thing and the by-year table doing another
